member.name: T:Kjs.AppLife.Update.Engine.Core.UpdateAction
member.summary: Provides the base implementation for all actions that are performed in an AppLife Update action list update.

remarks.para: To create a custom action, inherit from , provide a public parameterless constructor and implementations for and .

For storage in projects and in update packages, actions are serialized using an . In general, public read-write properties and fields will be automatically serialized. See the documentation for more information on serialization.

When an update is performed, the following steps are taken in order:
All actions are deserialized.
is called on every action in order.
is called on every action in order.
is called on every action in order.
If any error occurs when calling , is called on all actions that completed in reverse order.
If any error occurs when calling , is called on all actions that completed in reverse order, then is called on all actions in reverse order.
Errors in are ignored.
should contain the primary task performed by the action, and should reverse the effect of that task.
should contain any preparation that needs to be performed before any actions execute, and can throw an exception to abort the update before any changes are made. should reverse the effect of .
should perform nonessential cleanup that cannot be performed until the update has succeeded.

All five of these methods can optionally call to report progress from 0 to 100 percent. If no progress events are raised in this way, AppLife Update will automatically report 100% progress for each method when it returns.

Custom actions will appear in the action palette automatically when an assembly that they reside in is added in the AppLife update creation application. The default editor for custom actions uses a and so only public read-write properties can be edited. To use a custom editor for an action, provide an on the action and specify the type of
to use. An can also perform work when building the update package (such as copying files to go with the update) and customize the action's appearance in the action list.

To customize an action's appearance in the action palette, you can provide an on the action and specify the type of to use. Alternatively, you can specify one or more of the following attributes on the action, which will be automatically used by the default :
